import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Data
N_customers = 15
N_vehicles = 3
N_days = 5
capacity = 200
N = N_customers  # for MTZ

# Customer IDs
customers = list(range(1, N_customers + 1))

# Delivery frequency groups
daily_customers = [1, 2, 3]
otherday_customers = [4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
weekly_customers = [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]

# Demand per customer
demand = [0, 25, 30, 20, 15, 35, 40, 18, 22, 28, 32, 19, 21, 26, 24, 23]

# Distance matrix (0..15)
dist = [
    [0, 12, 18, 9, 15, 22, 7, 14, 20, 11, 16, 8, 13, 19, 10, 17],
    [12, 0, 6, 15, 21, 8, 17, 23, 10, 19, 4, 16, 5, 11, 18, 7],
    [18, 6, 0, 21, 3, 14, 9, 15, 12, 5, 10, 7, 13, 8, 4, 11],
    [9, 15, 21, 0, 18, 11, 16, 22, 7, 14, 20, 3, 19, 10, 17, 6],
    [15, 21, 3, 18, 0, 17, 12, 8, 15, 10, 7, 13, 4, 9, 14, 11],
    [22, 8, 14, 11, 17, 0, 19, 5, 12, 7, 14, 10, 17, 6, 13, 8],
    [7, 17, 9, 16, 12, 19, 0, 14, 21, 8, 15, 11, 18, 5, 12, 9],
    [14, 23, 15, 22, 8, 5, 14, 0, 17, 12, 9, 15, 6, 11, 16, 13],
    [20, 10, 12, 7, 15, 12, 21, 17, 0, 13, 18, 4, 19, 14, 9, 16],
    [11, 19, 5, 14, 10, 7, 8, 12, 13, 0, 15, 11, 6, 17, 12, 9],
    [16, 4, 10, 20, 7, 14, 15, 9, 18, 15, 0, 17, 8, 13, 18, 5],
    [8, 16, 7, 3, 13, 10, 11, 15, 4, 11, 17, 0, 14, 9, 16, 7],
    [13, 5, 13, 19, 4, 17, 18, 6, 19, 6, 8, 14, 0, 15, 10, 17],
    [19, 11, 8, 10, 9, 6, 5, 11, 14, 17, 13, 9, 15, 0, 7, 12],
    [10, 18, 4, 17, 14, 13, 12, 16, 9, 12, 18, 16, 10, 7, 0, 11],
    [17, 7, 11, 6, 11, 8, 9, 13, 16, 9, 5, 7, 17, 12, 11, 0]
]

# Environment and model
env = gp.Env()
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
serve = model.addVars(customers, range(N_days), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="serve")
y = model.addVars(N_vehicles, customers, range(N_days), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="y")
x = model.addVars(N_vehicles, range(16), range(16), range(N_days), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
u = model.addVars(N_vehicles, customers, range(N_days), vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")

# Serve constraints
for i in daily_customers:
    for t in range(N_days):
        model.addConstr(serve[i, t] == 1, name=f"daily_serve_{i}_{t}")
for i in otherday_customers:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(serve[i, t] for t in range(N_days)) == 2,
                    name=f"otherday_serve_{i}")
for i in weekly_customers:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(serve[i, t] for t in range(N_days)) == 1,
                    name=f"weekly_serve_{i}")

# Link y and serve
for v in range(N_vehicles):
    for i in customers:
        for t in range(N_days):
            model.addConstr(y[v, i, t] <= serve[i, t], name=f"y_le_serve_{v}_{i}_{t}")
            model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(y[v, i, t] for v in range(N_vehicles)) == serve[i, t],
                            name=f"serve_eq_sum_y_{i}_{t}")

# Flow constraints
for v in range(N_vehicles):
    for t in range(N_days):
        for i in customers:
            model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[v, i, j, t] for j in range(16) if j != i) == y[v, i, t],
                            name=f"outflow_{v}_{i}_{t}")
            model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[v, j, i, t] for j in range(16) if j != i) == y[v, i, t],
                            name=f"inflow_{v}_{i}_{t}")
        # Depot flow
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[v, 0, j, t] for j in range(1, 16)) ==
                        gp.quicksum(x[v, j, 0, t] for j in range(1, 16)),
                        name=f"depot_flow_{v}_{t}")
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[v, 0, j, t] for j in range(1, 16)) <= 1,
                        name=f"depot_use_{v}_{t}")

# Capacity constraints
for v in range(N_vehicles):
    for t in range(N_days):
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(demand[i] * y[v, i, t] for i in customers) <= capacity,
                        name=f"capacity_{v}_{t}")

# MTZ constraints
for v in range(N_vehicles):
    for t in range(N_days):
        for i in customers:
            model.addConstr(u[v, i, t] >= y[v, i, t], name=f"u_ge_y_{v}_{i}_{t}")
            model.addConstr(u[v, i, t] <= N * y[v, i, t], name=f"u_le_Ny_{v}_{i}_{t}")
        for i in customers:
            for j in customers:
                if i != j:
                    model.addConstr(u[v, i, t] - u[v, j, t] + N * x[v, i, j, t] <= N - 1,
                                    name=f"mtz_{v}_{i}_{j}_{t}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
model.setObjective(
    gp.quicksum(dist[i][j] * x[v, i, j, t]
                for v in range(N_vehicles)
                for i in range(16)
                for j in range(16)
                if i != j
                for t in range(N_days)),
    GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Suppress solver output
model.Params.OutputFlag = 0

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal}")

The company has forecasted component demands and wants to minimize total procurement cost while ensuring: (1) at least 60% of each component comes from suppliers with reliability ≥0.8, (2) no more than 40% of total spend goes to any single supplier, and (3) all demand is met. The quarterly demand is [1200, 800, 1500, 900, 600] units for C1-C5 respectively. Supplier data: S1 offers prices [12,15,18,20,22] $/unit with reliability 0.85 and capacity 2000 units; S2 offers [14,16,17,19,21] $/unit with reliability 0.75 and capacity 1800 units; S3 offers [13,14,19,18,20] $/unit with with reliability 0.90 and capacity 2500 units.

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create environment and model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Sets
suppliers = ['S1', 'S2', 'S3']
components = ['C1', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4', 'C5']

# Parameters
prices = {
    'S1': [12, 15, 18, 20, 22],
    'S2': [14, 16, 17, 19, 21],
    'S3': [13, 14, 19, 18, 20]
}
reliability = {
    'S1': 0.85,
    'S2': 0.75,
    'S3': 0.90
}
capacity = {
    'S1': 2000,
    'S2': 1800,
    'S3': 2500
}
demand = {
    'C1': 1200,
    'C2': 800,
    'C3': 1500,
    'C4': 900,
    'C5': 600
}

# Decision variables: procurement amounts
x = {}
for s in suppliers:
    for c in components:
        x[s, c] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"x_{s}_{c}")

# Total spend variable
total_spend = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="total_spend")

# Objective: minimize total cost
model.setObjective(
    gp.quicksum(prices[s][components.index(c)] * x[s, c] for s in suppliers for c in components),
    GRB.MINIMIZE
)

# Demand satisfaction constraints
for c in components:
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[s, c] for s in suppliers) == demand[c],
        name=f"demand_{c}"
    )

# Reliability constraints (at least 60% from reliable suppliers)
for c in components:
    reliable_suppliers = [s for s in suppliers if reliability[s] >= 0.8]
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[s, c] for s in reliable_suppliers) >= 0.6 * demand[c],
        name=f"reliability_{c}"
    )

# Supplier capacity constraints
for s in suppliers:
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[s, c] for c in components) <= capacity[s],
        name=f"capacity_{s}"
    )

# Total spend definition
model.addConstr(
    total_spend == gp.quicksum(prices[s][components.index(c)] * x[s, c] for s in suppliers for c in components),
    name="total_spend_def"
)

# Spend distribution constraint: no more than 40% to any single supplier
for s in suppliers:
    supplier_spend = gp.quicksum(prices[s][components.index(c)] * x[s, c] for c in components)
    model.addConstr(
        supplier_spend <= 0.4 * total_spend,
        name=f"spend_limit_{s}"
    )

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if found
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Build the model using the runtime-provided environment
m = gp.Model(env=env)

# Define the network edges with capacities (in thousand cubic meters/day)
edges = [
    ("A", "B", 15),
    ("A", "C", 10),
    ("B", "C", 5),
    ("B", "D", 10),
    ("C", "E", 8),
    ("C", "F", 12),
    ("E", "D", 7),
    ("F", "D", 20),
    ("G", "D", 0)   # G is out of service
]

# All nodes in the network
nodes = {"A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"}

# Intermediate nodes (excluding source A and sink D)
intermediate = nodes - {"A", "D"}

# Decision variables: flow on each directed edge
flow = {}
for (i, j, cap) in edges:
    var = m.addVar(lb=0, ub=cap, name=f"f_{i}_{j}")
    flow[(i, j)] = var

# Variable for the total flow from source to sink
flow_value = m.addVar(lb=0, name="flow_value")

# Flow conservation constraints for intermediate nodes
for n in intermediate:
    inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if j == n)
    outflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if i == n)
    m.addConstr(inflow == outflow, name=f"conserve_{n}")

# Source A: outflow - inflow = flow_value
source_inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if j == "A")
source_outflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if i == "A")
m.addConstr(source_outflow - source_inflow == flow_value, name="source_conserve")

# Sink D: inflow - outflow = flow_value
sink_inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if j == "D")
sink_outflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j)] for (i, j, _) in edges if i == "D")
m.addConstr(sink_inflow - sink_outflow == flow_value, name="sink_conserve")

# Objective: maximize the total flow from A to D
m.setObjective(flow_value, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

# Optimize the model
m.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if the solution is optimal
if m.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={m.objVal}")

|:--------------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create environment and model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Sets
customers = [1, 2, 3, 4]
trucks = [1, 2, 3]

# Processing times (hours)
p = {
    (1, 1): 2, (1, 2): 3, (1, 3): 1,
    (2, 1): 4, (2, 2): 2, (2, 3): 3,
    (3, 1): 1, (3, 2): 5, (3, 3): 2,
    (4, 1): 3, (4, 2): 2, (4, 3): 4
}

# Decision variables: start times
s = {}
for i in customers:
    for j in trucks:
        s[i, j] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, lb=0, name=f"s_{i}_{j}")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, lb=0, name="Cmax")

# Big-M value
M = 1000

# Makespan constraints
for i in customers:
    for j in trucks:
        model.addConstr(Cmax >= s[i, j] + p[i, j])

# Truck constraints (no overlap on same truck)
for j in trucks:
    for i in customers:
        for k in customers:
            if i < k:
                y = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"truck_{j}_{i}_{k}")
                model.addConstr(s[i, j] + p[i, j] <= s[k, j] + (1 - y) * M)
                model.addConstr(s[k, j] + p[k, j] <= s[i, j] + y * M)

# Customer constraints (no overlap across trucks for same customer)
for i in customers:
    for j in trucks:
        for l in trucks:
            if j < l:
                y = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"cust_{i}_{j}_{l}")
                model.addConstr(s[i, j] + p[i, j] <= s[i, l] + (1 - y) * M)
                model.addConstr(s[i, l] + p[i, l] <= s[i, j] + y * M)

# Objective: minimize makespan
model.setObjective(Cmax, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the final objective if optimal
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

from gurobipy import GRB

def main():
    # Parameters
    suppliers = ['S1', 'S2', 'S3']
    warehouses = ['W1', 'W2']
    customers = ['C1', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4']

    supplier_capacity = [120, 150, 90]
    customer_demand = [80, 60, 70, 90]

    cost_direct = [
        [8, 10, 12, 14],
        [9, 7, 11, 13],
        [11, 9, 8, 10]
    ]

    cost_first = [
        [4, 5],
        [6, 3],
        [5, 4]
    ]

    cost_second = [
        [6, 5, 7, 9],
        [7, 6, 5, 8]
    ]

    throughput = [200, 180]
    handling_cost = 2

    # Model
    m = gp.Model(env=env)

    # Decision variables
    x = {}
    for i in range(len(suppliers)):
        for j in range(len(customers)):
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

    y = {}
    for i in range(len(suppliers)):
        for k in range(len(warehouses)):
            y[i, k] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"y_{i}_{k}")

    z = {}
    for k in range(len(warehouses)):
        for j in range(len(customers)):
            z[k, j] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"z_{k}_{j}")

    m.update()

    # Constraints
    # Supplier capacity
    for i in range(len(suppliers)):
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(len(customers))) +
            gp.quicksum(y[i, k] for k in range(len(warehouses))) <= supplier_capacity[i],
            name=f"cap_s_{i}"
        )

    # Warehouse throughput
    for k in range(len(warehouses)):
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(y[i, k] for i in range(len(suppliers))) <= throughput[k],
            name=f"through_k_{k}"
        )

    # Flow conservation at warehouses
    for k in range(len(warehouses)):
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(y[i, k] for i in range(len(suppliers))) ==
            gp.quicksum(z[k, j] for j in range(len(customers))),
            name=f"flow_k_{k}"
        )

    # Customer demand
    for j in range(len(customers)):
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(len(suppliers))) +
            gp.quicksum(z[k, j] for k in range(len(warehouses))) == customer_demand[j],
            name=f"demand_c_{j}"
        )

    # Objective
    obj = (
        gp.quicksum(cost_direct[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(len(suppliers)) for j in range(len(customers))) +
        gp.quicksum(cost_first[i][k] * y[i, k] for i in range(len(suppliers)) for k in range(len(warehouses))) +
        gp.quicksum(cost_second[k][j] * z[k, j] for k in range(len(warehouses)) for j in range(len(customers))) +
        gp.quicksum(handling_cost * gp.quicksum(y[i, k] for i in range(len(suppliers))) for k in range(len(warehouses)))
    )
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Optimize
    m.optimize()

    if m.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={m.objVal}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create environment and model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Sets
products = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']
stores = ['Store1', 'Store2', 'Store3']
trucks = range(4)  # 0,1,2,3

# Parameters
weight = {'A': 2, 'B': 3, 'C': 1, 'D': 4, 'E': 2}
capacity = 15

# Demand dictionary: (store, product) -> quantity
demand = {
    ('Store1', 'A'): 2, ('Store1', 'B'): 1, ('Store1', 'C'): 3,
    ('Store2', 'A'): 1, ('Store2', 'D'): 2, ('Store2', 'E'): 1,
    ('Store3', 'B'): 3, ('Store3', 'C'): 2, ('Store3', 'E'): 1
}

# Decision variables
# x[p,t,s] = units of product p delivered to store s by truck t
x = model.addVars(products, trucks, stores, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")

# y[t] = 1 if truck t is used, 0 otherwise
y = model.addVars(trucks, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="y")

# Constraints
# Meet demand for each store and product
for s in stores:
    for p in products:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[p, t, s] for t in trucks) == demand.get((s, p), 0),
            name=f"demand_{s}_{p}"
        )

# Capacity constraints for each truck
for t in trucks:
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(weight[p] * x[p, t, s] for p in products for s in stores) <= capacity * y[t],
        name=f"capacity_{t}"
    )

# Objective: minimize number of trucks used
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(y[t] for t in trucks), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if solution is found
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={int(round(model.objVal))}")
```

# Store 6

    (3, 6): (10, 6),

costs = {arc: cst for arc, (_, cst) in arc_data.items()}

# Demands at stores (node, product) -> amount

demands[(4, 'B')] = 2
demands[(4, 'C')] = 3
# Store 5

demands[(5, 'D')] = 5
demands[(5, 'E')] = 3
# Store 6
demands[(6, 'A')] = 2
demands[(6, 'C')] = 3
demands[(6, 'E')] = 5

model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for p in products) <= capacities[(i, j)],

    inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if j == 1)
    model.addConstr(inflow == 0, name=f"warehouse_in_{p}")

total_out = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if i == 1 for p in products)

for n in [4, 5, 6]:
    for p in products:
        inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if j == n)
        outflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if i == n)
        model.addConstr(outflow == 0, name=f"store_{n}_out_{p}")
        model.addConstr(inflow == demands[(n, p)], name=f"store_{n}_in_{p}")

# Intermediate node constraints (2 and 3): flow conservation per product
for n in [2, 3]:
    for p in products:
        inflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if j == n)
        outflow = gp.quicksum(flow[(i, j, p)] for (i, j) in arcs if i == n)
        model.addConstr(inflow == outflow, name=f"node_{n}_conserve_{p}")

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output result
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def main():
    # Cost matrix (USD)
    cost = [
        [120, 150, 180, 90],
        [110, 140, 170, 80],
        [130, 160, 190, 100],
        [140, 170, 200, 110]
    ]
    n = 4  # number of trucks / locations

    # Create model with the provided environment
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    # Decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if truck i is assigned to location j
    x = model.addVars(n, n, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    # Each truck is assigned to exactly one location
    for i in range(n):
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(n)) == 1, name=f"truck_{i}")

    # Each location receives exactly one truck
    for j in range(n):
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(n)) == 1, name=f"loc_{j}")

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Solve the model
    model.optimize()

    # Output the optimal objective value
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def main():
    env = gp.Env()
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    routes = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    distance = {1: 1200, 2: 1800, 3: 900, 4: 1200, 5: 1800, 6: 900}
    demand = {1: 6500, 2: 7200, 3: 4800, 4: 5100, 5: 6200, 6: 3900}
    rev_per_teu = {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 90, 4: 110, 5: 140, 6: 80}

    # Decision variables: number of ships assigned to each route
    x = model.addVars(routes, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="ships")

    # Demand satisfaction and ship count limits per route
    for r in routes:
        model.addConstr(8000 * x[r] >= demand[r], name=f"demand_{r}")
        model.addConstr(x[r] <= (demand[r] + 7999) // 8000, name=f"max_ships_{r}")

    # Total ships available (12 total, at least 2 in reserve)
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[r] for r in routes) <= 10, name="total_ships")

    # Objective: maximize net profit
    revenue = gp.quicksum(demand[r] * rev_per_teu[r] * x[r] for r in routes)
    fuel_cost = gp.quicksum(0.2 * distance[r] * 600 * x[r] for r in routes)
    profit = revenue - fuel_cost
    model.setObjective(profit, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

    model.optimize()

    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={int(profit.getValue())}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

def main():
    env = gp.Env()
    model = gp.Model(env=env)

    vessels = {
        'A': {'a': 0.005, 'b': 0.1,  'c': 1.2,  'co2': 3.2,  'fixed': 500000},
        'B': {'a': 0.004, 'b': 0.08, 'c': 1.5,  'co2': 3.15, 'fixed': 600000},
        'C': {'a': 0.006, 'b': 0.12, 'c': 1.0,  'co2': 3.25, 'fixed': 450000},
    }

    distance = 6000.0          # nautical miles
    time_limit = 288.0         # hours

    # Decision variables
    y = model.addVars(vessels.keys(), vtype=GRB.BINARY, name='y')
    v = model.addVars(vessels.keys(), lb=1e-6, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name='v')

    # Exactly one vessel must be selected
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(y[i] for i in vessels) == 1, name='select_one')

    # Speed must be high enough to finish within the time limit if selected
    for i in vessels:
        model.addConstr(v[i] >= distance / time_limit * y[i], name=f'speed_min_{i}')

    # Allow non‑convex expressions
    model.Params.NonConvex = 2

    # Objective: minimize total cost
    cost_expr = 0
    for i, params in vessels.items():

        co2, fixed = params['co2'], params['fixed']

        fuel_rate = a * v[i] * v[i] + b * v[i] + c
        time_expr = distance / v[i]

        total_cost_i = fixed + fuel_cost + co2_cost

        cost_expr += y[i] * total_cost_i

    model.setObjective(cost_expr, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    model.optimize()

    if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

emissions_old = [15, 16, 14, 18, 17]                # Annual emissions (tons)

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Sets
docks = ['I1', 'I2', 'I3', 'I4', 'O1', 'O2', 'O3']
zone_of = {
    'I1': 'A', 'I2': 'A', 'O1': 'A',
    'I3': 'B', 'I4': 'B', 'O2': 'B', 'O3': 'B'
}
shipments = ['S1', 'S2', 'S3', 'S4', 'R1', 'R2', 'R3']
items = {
    'S1': 200, 'S2': 150, 'S3': 180, 'S4': 220,
    'R1': 250, 'R2': 300, 'R3': 200
}

# Congestion coefficients
coeff = {'A': 0.00005, 'B': 0.00004}
base_cost_per_item = 0.1

# Environment and model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: x[s,d] = 1 if shipment s assigned to dock d
x = {}
for s in shipments:
    for d in docks:
        x[s, d] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{s}_{d}")

# Each shipment assigned to exactly one dock
for s in shipments:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[s, d] for d in docks) == 1, name=f"ship_{s}")

# Each dock assigned to exactly one shipment
for d in docks:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[s, d] for s in shipments) == 1, name=f"dock_{d}")

# Total items per zone
total_items_zone = {}
for z in ['A', 'B']:
    total_items_zone[z] = gp.quicksum(
        items[s] * x[s, d]
        for s in shipments
        for d in docks
        if zone_of[d] == z
    )

# Objective: base handling cost + congestion cost
base_cost = gp.quicksum(base_cost_per_item * items[s] for s in shipments)
congestion_cost = gp.quicksum(
    coeff[z] * total_items_zone[z] * total_items_zone[z]
    for z in ['A', 'B']
)
model.setObjective(base_cost + congestion_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value
print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal}")

if __name__ == "__main__":

if __name__ == "__main__":

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create environment and model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Sets
zones = ['A', 'B', 'C']
vans = [1, 2]

# Parameters
demand = {'A': 120, 'B': 120, 'C': 90}
capacity = {1: 150, 2: 180}
dispatch_cost = {1: 300, 2: 320}
coeff = {1: 0.08, 2: 0.07}

# Decision variables
y = model.addVars(vans, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="y")  # van used
N = model.addVars(vans, zones, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="N")  # batteries replaced

# Constraints
# Capacity constraints
for i in vans:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(N[i, z] for z in zones) <= capacity[i], name=f"cap_{i}")

# Link usage to assignments
for i in vans:
    for z in zones:
        model.addConstr(N[i, z] <= capacity[i] * y[i], name=f"link_{i}_{z}")

# Demand satisfaction
for z in zones:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(N[i, z] for i in vans) == demand[z], name=f"demand_{z}")

# Objective: fixed dispatch cost + variable operational cost
obj = gp.quicksum(dispatch_cost[i] * y[i] for i in vans) + \
      gp.quicksum(coeff[i] * N[i, z] * N[i, z] for i in vans for z in zones)
model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value
print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")

import math
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Problem data
coords = [
    (0, 0),      # depot
    (3, 5),      # 1
    (5, 8),      # 2
    (2, 1),      # 3
    (8, 6),      # 4
    (4, 2),      # 5
    (9, 8),      # 6
    (1, 9),      # 7
    (1, 3),      # 8
    (6, 4),      # 9
    (7, 1)       # 10
]
service_time = [0, 5, 8, 5, 10, 6, 7, 9, 5, 12, 6]  # minutes
# Desired window centers in minutes after 8:30
center = [0,
          75,   # 9:30-10:00
          100,  # 10:00-10:20
          40,   # 9:00-9:20
          135,  # 10:30-11:00
          90,   # 9:45-10:15
          177.5,# 11:15-11:40
          115,  # 10:10-10:40
          57.5, # 9:15-9:40
          125,  # 10:20-10:50
          160]  # 11:00-11:20

n = 10  # number of customers
N = n + 1  # including depot

# Compute distance and travel time matrices
dist = [[0.0]*N for _ in range(N)]
travel_time = [[0.0]*N for _ in range(N)]
for i in range(N):
    xi, yi = coords[i]
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j:
            continue
        xj, yj = coords[j]
        d = math.hypot(xi - xj, yi - yj)
        dist[i][j] = d
        travel_time[i][j] = 2 * d  # 30 km/h => 0.5 km per minute => 2 * distance minutes

# Big M for time constraints
M = 1000.0

# Create model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(N, N, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
t = model.addVars(N, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="t")
u = model.addVars(N, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="u")

# Fix depot variables
model.addConstr(t[0] == 0, "t0")
model.addConstr(u[0] == 0, "u0")

# No self loops
for i in range(N):
    model.addConstr(x[i, i] == 0, f"no_loop_{i}")

# Each node has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in range(N):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(N)) == 1, f"out_{i}")

# Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
for j in range(1, N):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(N)) == 1, f"in_{j}")

# Return to depot once
model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, 0] for i in range(N)) == 1, "return_depot")

# Subtour elimination (MTZ)
for i in range(1, N):
    model.addConstr(u[i] >= 1, f"u_low_{i}")
    model.addConstr(u[i] <= n, f"u_up_{i}")
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j or i == 0 or j == 0:
            continue
        model.addConstr(u[i] - u[j] + (n + 1) * x[i, j] <= n, f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

# Time constraints
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j:
            continue
        model.addConstr(
            t[j] >= t[i] + service_time[i] + travel_time[i][j] - M * (1 - x[i, j]),
            f"time_{i}_{j}"
        )

# Objective: travel cost + penalty
linear = gp.quicksum(5 * dist[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(N) for j in range(N))
quadratic = gp.quicksum(0.2 * (t[i] - center[i]) * (t[i] - center[i]) for i in range(1, N))
model.setObjective(linear + quadratic, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output final objective if optimal
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.6f}")

import math
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Problem data
coords = [
    (0, 0),      # depot
    (3, 5),      # 1
    (5, 8),      # 2
    (2, 1),      # 3
    (8, 6),      # 4
    (4, 2),      # 5
    (9, 8),      # 6
    (1, 9),      # 7
    (1, 3),      # 8
    (6, 4),      # 9
    (7, 1)       # 10
]
service_time = [0, 5, 8, 5, 10, 6, 7, 9, 5, 12, 6]  # minutes
# Desired window centers in minutes after 8:30
center = [0,
          75,   # 9:30-10:00
          100,  # 10:00-10:20
          40,   # 9:00-9:20
          135,  # 10:30-11:00
          90,   # 9:45-10:15
          177.5,# 11:15-11:40
          115,  # 10:10-10:40
          57.5, # 9:15-9:40
          125,  # 10:20-10:50
          160]  # 11:00-11:20

n = 10  # number of customers
N = n + 1  # including depot

# Compute distance and travel time matrices
dist = [[0.0]*N for _ in range(N)]
travel_time = [[0.0]*N for _ in range(N)]
for i in range(N):
    xi, yi = coords[i]
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j:
            continue
        xj, yj = coords[j]
        d = math.hypot(xi - xj, yi - yj)
        dist[i][j] = d
        travel_time[i][j] = 2 * d  # 30 km/h => 0.5 km per minute => 2 * distance minutes

# Big M for time constraints
M = 1000.0

# Create model
env = gp.Env(empty=True)
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(N, N, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
t = model.addVars(N, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="t")
u = model.addVars(N, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="u")

# Fix depot variables
model.addConstr(t[0] == 0, "t0")
model.addConstr(u[0] == 0, "u0")

# No self loops
for i in range(N):
    model.addConstr(x[i, i] == 0, f"no_loop_{i}")

# Each node has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in range(N):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(N)) == 1, f"out_{i}")

# Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
for j in range(1, N):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(N)) == 1, f"in_{j}")

# Return to depot once
model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, 0] for i in range(N)) == 1, "return_depot")

# Subtour elimination (MTZ)
for i in range(1, N):
    model.addConstr(u[i] >= 1, f"u_low_{i}")
    model.addConstr(u[i] <= n, f"u_up_{i}")
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j or i == 0 or j == 0:
            continue
        model.addConstr(u[i] - u[j] + (n + 1) * x[i, j] <= n, f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

# Time constraints
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j:
            continue
        model.addConstr(
            t[j] >= t[i] + service_time[i] + travel_time[i][j] - M * (1 - x[i, j]),
            f"time_{i}_{j}"
        )

# Objective: travel cost + penalty
linear = gp.quicksum(5 * dist[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(N) for j in range(N))
quadratic = gp.quicksum(0.2 * (t[i] - center[i]) * (t[i] - center[i]) for i in range(1, N))
model.setObjective(linear + quadratic, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output final objective if optimal
if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.6f}")

from gurobipy import GRB

# Define data
zones = ['Commercial Center', 'University City', 'Tech Park', 'Tourist Area', 'Transit Hub']
attractiveness = {
    'Commercial Center': 500,
    'University City': 800,
    'Tech Park': 700,
    'Tourist Area': 600,
    'Transit Hub': 900
}
total_fleet = 1000
total_attr = sum(attractiveness[z] for z in zones)

# Ideal deployment for each zone
ideal = {z: total_fleet * attractiveness[z] / total_attr for z in zones}

# Minimum quota for each zone (10% weighted)
min_quota = {z: 0.1 * total_fleet * attractiveness[z] / total_attr for z in zones}

# Create environment and model
env = gp.Env()
env.start()
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: number of scooters in each zone (integer)
x = {z: model.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=z) for z in zones}

# Constraints
model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[z] for z in zones) == total_fleet, name='total_fleet')

for z in zones:
    model.addConstr(x[z] >= min_quota[z], name=f'min_{z}')

# Absolute difference between Commercial Center and Transit Hub
model.addConstr(gp.abs(x['Commercial Center'] - x['Transit Hub']) <= 50, name='adjacent_diff')

# Cluster constraints
cluster1 = ['Commercial Center', 'Tourist Area']
cluster2 = ['University City', 'Tech Park', 'Transit Hub']
model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[z] for z in cluster1) <= 600, name='cluster1_max')
model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[z] for z in cluster2) <= 600, name='cluster2_max')

# Objective: minimize sum of squared differences from ideal deployment
obj_expr = gp.quicksum((x[z] - ideal[z]) * (x[z] - ideal[z]) for z in zones)
model.setObjective(obj_expr, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value
print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.objVal}")
```

berths = ['B1','B2','B3']

z = model.addVars(deps, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name='z')

# Constraints
M = 1000
epsilon = 0.1

    model.addConstr(e[sh] == s[sh] + dur[sh], name=f'duration_{sh}')
    model.addConstr(e[sh] <= 72, name=f'horizon_{sh}')
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[sh,b] for b in berths) == 1, name=f'berth_assign_{sh}')

                                name=f'order2_{i}_{j}_{b}')

    model.addConstr(s[dep] >= e[pred], name=f'dep_{pred}_{dep}')
    model.addConstr(s[dep] - e[pred] <= 2 + M*(1 - z[pred,dep]), name=f'bonus1_{pred}_{dep}')

}

from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Flights and gates
flights = ['F1', 'F2', 'F3', 'F4']
gates   = ['G1', 'G2']

# Parameters
arrival = [600, 630, 675, 645]          # minutes from midnight
scheduled_departure = [660, 690, 750, 705]
M = 200  # big-M

flight_index = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(flights)}

# Decision variables
x = {}
for f in flights:
    for g in gates:
        x[(f, g)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{f}_{g}")

d = {}
for f in flights:
    d[f] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"d_{f}")

# Each flight assigned to exactly one gate
for f in flights:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(f, g)] for g in gates) == 1, name=f"assign_{f}")

# Pairwise non‑overlap constraints
y = {}
for i in range(len(flights)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(flights)):
        f = flights[i]
        g = flights[j]
        for gate in gates:
            # Binary variable indicating f before g on this gate
            y[(f, g, gate)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # y <= x_f_gate, y <= x_g_gate
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] <= x[(f, gate)], name=f"y_le_x_f_{f}_{g}_{gate}")
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] <= x[(g, gate)], name=f"y_le_x_g_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # y >= x_f_gate + x_g_gate - 1
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] >= x[(f, gate)] + x[(g, gate)] - 1,
                            name=f"y_ge_xsum_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # Departure times
            dep_f = scheduled_departure[flight_index[f]] + d[f]
            dep_g = scheduled_departure[flight_index[g]] + d[g]
            arr_f = arrival[flight_index[f]]
            arr_g = arrival[flight_index[g]]

            # If f before g: dep_f <= arr_g
            model.addConstr(dep_f <= arr_g + M * (1 - y[(f, g, gate)]) +
                            M * (1 - x[(f, gate)]) + M * (1 - x[(g, gate)]),
                            name=f"order1_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # If g before f: dep_g <= arr_f
            model.addConstr(dep_g <= arr_f + M * y[(f, g, gate)] +
                            M * (1 - x[(f, gate)]) + M * (1 - x[(g, gate)]),
                            name=f"order2_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

# Objective: minimize total delay
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(d[f] for f in flights), GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

model = gp.Model(env=env)

gates   = ['G1', 'G2']

# Parameters

scheduled_departure = [660, 690, 750, 705]
M = 200  # big-M

flight_index = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(flights)}

# Decision variables

for f in flights:
    for g in gates:
        x[(f, g)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{f}_{g}")

d = {}
for f in flights:
    d[f] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"d_{f}")

# Each flight assigned to exactly one gate
for f in flights:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(f, g)] for g in gates) == 1, name=f"assign_{f}")

# Pairwise non‑overlap constraints
y = {}
for i in range(len(flights)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(flights)):
        f = flights[i]
        g = flights[j]
        for gate in gates:
            # Binary variable indicating f before g on this gate
            y[(f, g, gate)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # y <= x_f_gate, y <= x_g_gate
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] <= x[(f, gate)], name=f"y_le_x_f_{f}_{g}_{gate}")
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] <= x[(g, gate)], name=f"y_le_x_g_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # y >= x_f_gate + x_g_gate - 1
            model.addConstr(y[(f, g, gate)] >= x[(f, gate)] + x[(g, gate)] - 1,
                            name=f"y_ge_xsum_{f}_{g}_{gate}")

            # Departure times
            dep_f = scheduled_departure[flight_index[f]] + d[f]
            dep_g = scheduled_departure[flight_index[g]] + d[g]
            arr_f = arrival[flight_index[f]]
            arr_g = arrival[flight_index[g]]

            # If f before g: dep_f <= arr_g
            model.addConstr(dep_f <= arr_g + M * (1 - y[(f, g, gate)]) +

# Objective: minimize total delay

# Data

lengths = [287,196,261,288,208,238,190,217,254]
opt_pos = [375,419,591,510,567,64,507,377,93]
dev_cost = [8,4,5,5,2,6,8,6,8]

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: berth start positions (integer)
s = {}
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    s[name] = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=900-lengths[i], vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"s_{name}")

# Deviation variables
d = {}
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    d[name] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"d_{name}")

# Pairwise non-overlap constraints
M = 900
for i in range(len(names)):
    for j in range(i+1, len(names)):
        name_i = names[i]
        name_j = names[j]
        # Binary variable: 1 if i before j
        y = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{name_i}_{name_j}")
        # If y==1 then i before j
        model.addConstr(s[name_i] + lengths[i] <= s[name_j] + M*(1 - y), name=f"order1_{name_i}_{name_j}")
        # If y==0 then j before i
        model.addConstr(s[name_j] + lengths[j] <= s[name_i] + M*y, name=f"order2_{name_i}_{name_j}")

# Deviation constraints
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    model.addConstr(d[name] >= s[name] - opt_pos[i], name=f"dev_pos1_{name}")
    model.addConstr(d[name] >= opt_pos[i] - s[name], name=f"dev_pos2_{name}")

# Objective: minimize total deviation cost
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(dev_cost[i] * d[name] for i, name in enumerate(names)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

from gurobipy import GRB

# Data
names = ['A','B','C','D','E','F','G','H','I']
lengths = [287,196,261,288,208,238,190,217,254]
opt_pos = [375,419,591,510,567,64,507,377,93]
dev_cost = [8,4,5,5,2,6,8,6,8]

# Decision variables: berth start positions (integer)

for i, name in enumerate(names):
    s[name] = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=900-lengths[i], vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"s_{name}")

# Deviation variables
d = {}
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    d[name] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"d_{name}")

# Pairwise non-overlap constraints
M = 900
for i in range(len(names)):
    for j in range(i+1, len(names)):
        name_i = names[i]
        name_j = names[j]
        # Binary variable: 1 if i before j
        y = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{name_i}_{name_j}")
        # If y==1 then i before j
        model.addConstr(s[name_i] + lengths[i] <= s[name_j] + M*(1 - y), name=f"order1_{name_i}_{name_j}")
        # If y==0 then j before i
        model.addConstr(s[name_j] + lengths[j] <= s[name_i] + M*y, name=f"order2_{name_i}_{name_j}")

# Deviation constraints
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    model.addConstr(d[name] >= s[name] - opt_pos[i], name=f"dev_pos1_{name}")

# Objective: minimize total deviation cost
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(dev_cost[i] * d[name] for i, name in enumerate(names)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X

    (0, 0),          # depot (node 0)
    (3, -8),         # 1
    (-10, -5),       # 2
    (3, 0),          # 3
    (-3, -3),        # 4

    (4, -5),         # 8

    (-6, -3),        #13
    (-8, -7),        #14
    (-1, 8)          #15
]

# Demand at each collection point (index 1..15)
demand = [0, 20, 20, 28, 12, 30, 24, 30, 12, 27, 26, 21, 20, 12, 16, 19]

# Parameters
num_trucks = 4
capacity = 100
max_distance = 45
n = 15  # number of collection points

# Precompute Euclidean distances
dist = [[0.0]*(n+1) for _ in range(n+1)]
for i in range(n+1):
    xi, yi = coords[i]
    for j in range(n+1):
        xj, yj = coords[j]
        dist[i][j] = math.hypot(xi - xj, yi - yj)

# Create model with provided environment
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: x[i,j,k] = 1 if truck k travels from i to j
x = {}
for k in range(num_trucks):
    for i in range(n+1):
        for j in range(n+1):
            if i == j:
                continue
            var = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{i}_{j}_{k}")
            x[(i, j, k)] = var

# Decision variables: u[i,k] position of node i in truck k's route
u = {}
for k in range(num_trucks):
    for i in range(1, n+1):
        var = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, lb=0, ub=n, name=f"u_{i}_{k}")
        u[(i, k)] = var

model.update()

# Constraints

# Each truck starts and ends at the depot
for k in range(num_trucks):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(0, j, k)] for j in range(n+1) if j != 0) == 1, name=f"start_{k}")
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(i, 0, k)] for i in range(n+1) if i != 0) == 1, name=f"end_{k}")

# Each collection point has exactly one incoming and one outgoing edge across all trucks
for i in range(1, n+1):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(i, j, k)] for k in range(num_trucks) for j in range(n+1) if j != i) == 1,
                    name=f"out_{i}")
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(j, i, k)] for k in range(num_trucks) for j in range(n+1) if j != i) == 1,
                    name=f"in_{i}")

# Subtour elimination (MTZ) and linking u with visit status
for k in range(num_trucks):
    for i in range(1, n+1):
        # u[i,k] <= n * sum_j x[i,j,k]
        model.addConstr(u[(i, k)] <= n * gp.quicksum(x[(i, j, k)] for j in range(n+1) if j != i),
                        name=f"u_leq_{i}_{k}")
        # u[i,k] >= sum_j x[i,j,k]
        model.addConstr(u[(i, k)] >= gp.quicksum(x[(i, j, k)] for j in range(n+1) if j != i),
                        name=f"u_geq_{i}_{k}")

    for i in range(1, n+1):
        for j in range(1, n+1):
            if i == j:
                continue
            # MTZ constraint
            model.addConstr(u[(i, k)] - u[(j, k)] + (n + 1) * x[(i, j, k)] <= n,
                            name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}_{k}")

# Capacity constraints for each truck
for k in range(num_trucks):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(demand[i] * gp.quicksum(x[(i, j, k)] for j in range(n+1) if j != i)
                                for i in range(1, n+1)) <= capacity,
                    name=f"cap_{k}")

# Distance limit for each truck
for k in range(num_trucks):
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(dist[i][j] * x[(i, j, k)]
                                for i in range(n+1) for j in range(n+1) if i != j) <= max_distance,
                    name=f"dist_{k}")

# Objective: minimize total driving distance
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(dist[i][j] * x[(i, j, k)]
                               for k in range(num_trucks)
                               for i in range(n+1)
                               for j in range(n+1) if i != j),
                   GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X

```python
import gurobipy as gp

model = gp.Model(env=env)

A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X

limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Demands for weeks 1 to 7
demands = [6, 9, 12, 8, 5, 7, 4]

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Long‑term lease (available all 7 weeks)
L = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="L")

# Short‑term lease per week
s = {}
for t in range(1, 8):
    s[t] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"s_{t}")

# Shared forklifts (available only weeks 2, 4, 5)
sh = {}
for t in [2, 4, 5]:
    sh[t] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"sh_{t}")

# Promotional forklifts (available weeks 4–7, max 2 per week)
p = {}
for t in [4, 5, 6, 7]:
    p[t] = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=2, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"p_{t}")

# Weekly demand constraints
for t in range(1, 8):
    expr = L + s[t]
    if t in sh:
        expr += sh[t]
    if t in p:
        expr += p[t]
    model.addConstr(expr >= demands[t-1], name=f"demand_{t}")

# Objective: minimize total leasing cost
cost = 240 * L
cost += gp.quicksum(390 * s[t] for t in range(1, 8))
cost += gp.quicksum(220 * sh[t] for t in sh)
cost += gp.quicksum(190 * p[t] for t in p)
model.setObjective(cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

s = {}

    s[t] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"s_{t}")

# Shared forklifts (available only weeks 2, 4, 5)
sh = {}
for t in [2, 4, 5]:
    sh[t] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"sh_{t}")

# Promotional forklifts (available weeks 4–7, max 2 per week)
p = {}
for t in [4, 5, 6, 7]:

    'J1': [('M1', 3), ('M2', 2), ('M5', 4)],
    'J2': [('M3', 4), ('M4', 3), ('M5', 2)],
    'J3': [('M2', 3), ('M1', 5), ('M4', 2)],
    'J4': [('M1', 2), ('M3', 3), ('M4', 4)]
}

# Create a list of all operations with unique ids
ops = []  # list of (job, op_index, machine, proc_time)
for job, steps in jobs.items():
    for idx, (machine, proc) in enumerate(steps, start=1):
        ops.append((job, idx, machine, proc))

# Map machine to list of operation indices
machine_ops = {}
for i, (_, _, machine, _) in enumerate(ops):
    machine_ops.setdefault(machine, []).append(i)

# Big M value
M = sum(proc for (_, _, _, proc) in ops) + 1  # 38

# Build the model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: start times
start = {}
for i, (job, op_idx, machine, proc) in enumerate(ops):
    start[i] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"s_{job}_{op_idx}")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="Cmax")

# Precedence constraints within each job
for job, steps in jobs.items():
    # Find indices of operations for this job
    job_ops = [i for i, (j, _, _, _) in enumerate(ops) if j == job]
    # Sort by operation index
    job_ops.sort(key=lambda i: ops[i][1])
    for k in range(len(job_ops)-1):
        i = job_ops[k]
        j = job_ops[k+1]
        proc_i = ops[i][3]
        model.addConstr(start[i] + proc_i <= start[j], name=f"prec_{job}_{k+1}")

# Machine constraints (disjunctive)
for machine, op_list in machine_ops.items():
    for a in range(len(op_list)):
        for b in range(a+1, len(op_list)):
            i = op_list[a]
            j = op_list[b]
            proc_i = ops[i][3]
            proc_j = ops[j][3]
            y = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{i}_{j}")
            # i before j
            model.addConstr(start[i] + proc_i <= start[j] + M * (1 - y), name=f"mach_{machine}_{i}_{j}_1")
            # j before i
            model.addConstr(start[j] + proc_j <= start[i] + M * y, name=f"mach_{machine}_{i}_{j}_2")

for i, (_, _, _, proc) in enumerate(ops):
    model.addConstr(start[i] + proc <= Cmax, name=f"makespan_{i}")

# Objective: minimize makespan
model.setObjective(Cmax, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

| 4       | 36,000               | 33,000               |

s = [model.addVar(lb=0, name=f"s{t}") for t in range(1, 7)]           # quantity sold
b = [model.addVar(lb=0, name=f"b{t}") for t in range(1, 7)]           # quantity bought

# Initial inventory
model.addConstr(I[0] == 150, name="init_inventory")

# Balance equations for subsequent quarters
for t in range(1, 6):  # t=1..5 corresponds to quarters 2..6
    model.addConstr(I[t] == I[t-1] - s[t-1] + b[t-1], name=f"balance_{t+1}")

# Constraints for each quarter
for t in range(6):
    model.addConstr(s[t] <= I[t], name=f"sell_limit_{t+1}")
    model.addConstr(b[t] <= 500 - (I[t] - s[t]), name=f"buy_limit_{t+1}")

# Objective: maximize total profit
model.setObjective(
    gp.quicksum(sell_price[t] * s[t] - buy_price[t] * b[t] for t in range(6)),
    GRB.MAXIMIZE
)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:

from gurobipy import GRB

# Sets
DCs = [1, 2, 3]
Hubs = [1, 2, 3]

# Parameters
standard = {1: 150, 2: 250, 3: 300}
premium  = {1: 30,  2: 100, 3: 70}
dist = {
    (1,1): 0,  (1,2): 12, (1,3): 18,
    (2,1): 12, (2,2): 0,  (2,3): 15,
    (3,1): 18, (3,2): 15, (3,3): 0
}

# Model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(DCs, Hubs, lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="std")
y = model.addVars(DCs, Hubs, lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="prem")
p = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="premium_per_hub")

# Constraints
for j in Hubs:
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[i,j] for i in DCs) + gp.quicksum(y[i,j] for i in DCs) == 300,
        name=f"total_inventory_{j}"
    )
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(y[i,j] for i in DCs) == p,
        name=f"premium_equal_{j}"

        gp.quicksum(x[i,j] for j in Hubs) <= standard[i],
        name=f"std_available_{i}"
    )
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(y[i,j] for j in Hubs) <= premium[i],
        name=f"prem_available_{i}"
    )

# Objective: minimize total transportation distance
obj = gp.quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * (x[i,j] + y[i,j]) for i in DCs for j in Hubs)
model.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Data
farms = ["A", "B", "C"]
stores = ["1", "2", "3", "4"]

prod_cost = [100, 120, 150]          # $/ton
capacity = [500, 400, 600]           # tons
water_use = [6, 8, 6]                # m³/ton
fert_use  = [5, 4, 3]                # kg/ton

trans_cost = [
    [20, 25, 30, 15],  # A
    [22, 26, 32, 18],  # B
    [18, 24, 28, 14]   # C
]

demand = [200, 300, 400, 500]        # tons

# Model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] = tons shipped from farm i to store j
x = {}
for i in range(len(farms)):
    for j in range(len(stores)):
        var_name = f"x_{farms[i]}_{stores[j]}"
        x[i, j] = model.addVar(lb=0, name=var_name)

# Supply capacity constraints
for i in range(len(farms)):
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(len(stores))) <= capacity[i],
        name=f"capacity_{farms[i]}"
    )

# Demand constraints (exact fulfillment)
for j in range(len(stores)):
    model.addConstr(
        gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in range(len(farms))) == demand[j],
        name=f"demand_{stores[j]}"
    )

# Sustainability constraints
# Water: average <= 7 m³/ton
water_coeff = [wu - 7 for wu in water_use]
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(water_coeff[i] * x[i, j] for i in range(len(farms)) for j in range(len(stores))) <= 0,
    name="water_sustainability"
)

# Fertilizer: average <= 4 kg/ton
fert_coeff = [fu - 4 for fu in fert_use]
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(fert_coeff[i] * x[i, j] for i in range(len(farms)) for j in range(len(stores))) <= 0,
    name="fert_sustainability"
)

# Objective: minimize total cost (production + transportation)
model.setObjective(
    gp.quicksum((prod_cost[i] + trans_cost[i][j]) * x[i, j]
                for i in range(len(farms)) for j in range(len(stores))),
    GRB.MINIMIZE
)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

from gurobipy import GRB

}

}
VI = {

}
flash = {
    'Alpha': 45,
    'Beta': 55,
    'Gamma': 60,
    'Delta': 40,
    'Epsilon': 50
}
boil = {
    'Alpha': 150,
    'Beta': 180,
    'Gamma': 200,
    'Delta': 130,
    'Epsilon': 160
}
density = {
    'Alpha': 0.85,
    'Beta': 0.92,
    'Gamma': 0.89,
    'Delta': 0.87,
    'Epsilon': 0.91
}

# Solvent data
solvents = ['Standard', 'Premium']
demand = {
    'Standard': 8500,
    'Premium': 25000
}
price = {
    'Standard': 25.50,
    'Premium': 28.75
}
VI_min = {
    'Standard': 85,
    'Premium': 92
}
boil_min = {
    'Standard': 140,
    'Premium': 140
}
flash_exact = 50
density_exact = 0.88
beta_fraction_limit = 0.35

# Create model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables: raw material usage per solvent
x = {(m, s): model.addVar(lb=0, name=f"x_{m}_{s}") for m in materials for s in solvents}

# Total volume of each solvent
V = {s: model.addVar(lb=0, name=f"V_{s}") for s in solvents}

# Constraints
for s in solvents:
    # Total volume equals sum of raw materials
    model.addConstr(V[s] == gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] for m in materials), name=f"volume_{s}")
    # Demand must be met
    model.addConstr(V[s] >= demand[s], name=f"demand_{s}")
    # Beta fraction limit
    model.addConstr(x[('Beta', s)] <= beta_fraction_limit * V[s], name=f"beta_frac_{s}")
    # Flash point exact
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] * flash[m] for m in materials) == flash_exact * V[s],
                    name=f"flash_{s}")
    # Density exact
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] * density[m] for m in materials) == density_exact * V[s],
                    name=f"density_{s}")
    # Viscosity index minimum
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] * VI[m] for m in materials) >= VI_min[s] * V[s],
                    name=f"VI_min_{s}")
    # Boiling point minimum
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] * boil[m] for m in materials) >= boil_min[s] * V[s],
                    name=f"boil_min_{s}")

# Raw material availability constraints (except Epsilon)
for m in materials:
    if m != 'Epsilon':
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[(m, s)] for s in solvents) <= availability[m],
                        name=f"avail_{m}")

# Objective: maximize profit (revenue - cost)
revenue = gp.quicksum(price[s] * V[s] for s in solvents)
cost_total = gp.quicksum(cost[m] * x[(m, s)] for m in materials for s in solvents)
model.setObjective(revenue - cost_total, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
R = model.addVar(lb=0, name="raw_units")                     # raw material units processed
EB_sold = model.addVar(lb=0, name="EB_sold")                 # Engine Block sold directly
EB_to_T = model.addVar(lb=0, name="EB_to_T")                 # Engine Block processed into Transmission
EB_to_B = model.addVar(lb=0, name="EB_to_B")                 # Engine Block processed into Brake System
T_sold = model.addVar(lb=0, name="T_sold")                   # Transmission sold directly
T_to_B = model.addVar(lb=0, name="T_to_B")                   # Transmission processed into Brake System

# Constraints
model.addConstr(EB_sold + EB_to_T + EB_to_B <= 7 * R, name="EB_availability")
model.addConstr(T_sold + T_to_B <= 3 * R + EB_to_T, name="T_availability")
model.addConstr(7 * R + 4 * EB_to_T + 6 * EB_to_B + 5 * T_to_B <= 60000, name="machine_time")
model.addConstr(EB_sold <= 20000, name="EB_demand")
model.addConstr(T_sold <= 15000, name="T_demand")
model.addConstr(EB_to_B + T_to_B <= 12000, name="Brake_demand")
model.addConstr(EB_to_B + T_to_B >= 4000, name="Brake_minimum")

# Objective: maximize profit
profit = (
    25 * EB_sold
    + 35 * T_sold
    + 35 * EB_to_B
    + 33 * T_to_B
    - 68 * R
    - 5 * EB_to_T
)
model.setObjective(profit, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

SupplyChain Logistics Co. is responsible for distributing two types of products, Product A and Product B. The company needs to meet the market demand for these two products across four quarters of the year (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) while aiming to minimize the total annual operating costs, which include labor costs and inventory holding costs. The company must decide the number of workers in each group, and this number remains constant throughout the year. Each on-duty worker, in a working quarter, can only choose to handle one type of product: either a maximum of 60 units of Product A or a maximum of 40 units of Product B. They cannot split their capacity to handle both products within the same quarter. The wage for each worker per working quarter is $600, so the annual wage for each worker is $1800.At the end of each quarter, an inventory holding cost of $70 per unit is incurred for any remaining product (either A or B) in the warehouse. It is assumed that at the beginning of the first quarter of the first year, the initial inventory for both Product A and Product B is 0 units. To simplify the model, it is assumed that at the end of the fourth quarter each year, the inventory for both Product A and Product B must be 0 units.The company's optimization objective is: to determine the number of workers in each rotation group and how to assign on-duty workers to produce Product A and Product B each quarter, in order to meet all quarterly product demands and minimize the total annual operating costs (including the total wages for all registered workers and the total inventory holding costs incurred at the end of all quarters).

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Worker groups (integer)
w = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"w{i+1}") for i in range(4)]

# Assignment of workers to products each quarter (integer)
xA = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"xA_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]
xB = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"xB_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]

# Inventory of products at end of each quarter (continuous, non‑negative)
invA = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"invA_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]
invB = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"invB_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]

# Demand for each product in each quarter
demandA = [800, 600, 700, 900]
demandB = [500, 400, 600, 300]

# Workers on duty each quarter (sum of the three groups not on leave)
workers_on_duty = [gp.quicksum(w[i] for i in range(4) if i != q) for q in range(4)]

# Production capacity constraints
for q in range(4):
    model.addConstr(xA[q] + xB[q] <= workers_on_duty[q], name=f"prod_cap_{q+1}")

# Inventory dynamics
for q in range(4):
    prodA = 60 * xA[q]
    prodB = 40 * xB[q]
    if q == 0:
        model.addConstr(invA[q] == prodA - demandA[q], name=f"invA_dyn_1")
        model.addConstr(invB[q] == prodB - demandB[q], name=f"invB_dyn_1")
    else:
        model.addConstr(invA[q] == invA[q-1] + prodA - demandA[q], name=f"invA_dyn_{q+1}")
        model.addConstr(invB[q] == invB[q-1] + prodB - demandB[q], name=f"invB_dyn_{q+1}")

# Inventory must be non‑negative (already enforced by lb=0) and zero at end of year
model.addConstr(invA[3] == 0, name="invA_end")
model.addConstr(invB[3] == 0, name="invB_end")

# Objective: minimize wages + inventory holding costs
total_wages = 1800 * gp.quicksum(w)
inventory_cost = 70 * gp.quicksum(invA[q] + invB[q] for q in range(4))
model.setObjective(total_wages + inventory_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Worker groups (integer)
w = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"w{i+1}") for i in range(4)]

# Assignment of workers to products each quarter (integer)
xA = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"xA_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]
xB = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"xB_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]

# Inventory of products at end of each quarter (continuous, non‑negative)
invA = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"invA_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]
invB = [model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"invB_{q+1}") for q in range(4)]

# Demand for each product in each quarter
demandA = [800, 600, 700, 900]
demandB = [500, 400, 600, 300]

# Workers on duty each quarter (sum of the three groups not on leave)
workers_on_duty = [gp.quicksum(w[i] for i in range(4) if i != q) for q in range(4)]

# Production capacity constraints
for q in range(4):
    model.addConstr(xA[q] + xB[q] <= workers_on_duty[q], name=f"prod_cap_{q+1}")

# Inventory dynamics
for q in range(4):

    prodB = 40 * xB[q]
    if q == 0:
        model.addConstr(invA[q] == prodA - demandA[q], name=f"invA_dyn_1")
        model.addConstr(invB[q] == prodB - demandB[q], name=f"invB_dyn_1")
    else:
        model.addConstr(invA[q] == invA[q-1] + prodA - demandA[q], name=f"invA_dyn_{q+1}")
        model.addConstr(invB[q] == invB[q-1] + prodB - demandB[q], name=f"invB_dyn_{q+1}")

# Inventory must be non‑negative (already enforced by lb=0) and zero at end of year
model.addConstr(invA[3] == 0, name="invA_end")
model.addConstr(invB[3] == 0, name="invB_end")

total_wages = 1800 * gp.quicksum(w)
inventory_cost = 70 * gp.quicksum(invA[q] + invB[q] for q in range(4))

TASK

Translate the problem into one complete Python program using gurobipy and solve

-----------------------

STEP 3: Produce the final output
--------------------------------

FINAL_OBJECTIVE=<finite numeric value>.

RULES
-----
Do not read or write files, access the network, spawn processes, install
packages, call input(), use dynamic evaluation, or revise the model after an
error. The caller performs policy checking and solver verification separately.

FEW-SHOT DEMONSTRATIONS

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 2
=========

Input
-----
An energy company chooses nonnegative integer numbers of solar and wind
projects. A solar project costs 7 units and a wind project costs 5 units. The
portfolio must satisfy 2 solar + 3 wind >= 10, while grid capacity requires
4 solar + wind <= 15. What is the minimum total investment cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
solar = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="solar")
wind = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="wind")
model.addConstr(2 * solar + 3 * wind >= 10, name="minimum_output")
model.addConstr(4 * solar + wind <= 15, name="grid_capacity")
model.setObjective(7 * solar + 5 * wind, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

END FEW-SHOT DEMONSTRATIONS

TARGET PROBLEM
--------------
Warehouse 24 operates around the clock to fulfill online orders. Workers are scheduled in two consecutive 6-hour shifts and are paid $12 per hour. The possible shifts are as follows: midnight–6 A.M., 6 A.M.–noon, noon–6 P.M., and 6 P.M.–midnight. During each shift, the following numbers of orders arrive: midnight–6 A.M., 150; 6 A.M.–noon, 250; noon–6 P.M., 400; 6 P.M.–midnight, 300. Each worker can process up to 60 orders per shift. To account for customer dissatisfaction due to delayed orders, any order that remains unprocessed at the end of a shift incurs a penalty of $1. The warehouse ensures that all orders received by midnight are processed by the start of the next day, so the midnight–6 A.M. shift begins with no pending orders. How can Warehouse 24 minimize the total cost of labor and customer dissatisfaction penalties while meeting its order processing requirements?

| Shift              | Orders Received |  
|--------------------|-----------------|  
| Midnight–6 A.M.    | 150             |  
| 6 A.M.–Noon        | 250             |  
| Noon–6 P.M.        | 400             |  
| 6 P.M.–Midnight    | 300             |

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create model with the provided environment
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Orders received in each shift
orders = [150, 250, 400, 300]

# Decision variables: number of workers scheduled for each pair of consecutive shifts
w1 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w1")  # midnight–6 AM & 6 AM–noon
w2 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w2")  # 6 AM–noon & noon–6 PM
w3 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w3")  # noon–6 PM & 6 PM–midnight

# Decision variables: orders processed and penalties for each shift
processed = []
penalty   = []
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    p = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"processed_{i}")
    pr = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"penalty_{i}")
    processed.append(p)
    penalty.append(pr)

# Capacity constraints for each shift
# Shift 1: midnight–6 AM
model.addConstr(processed[0] <= 60 * w1, name="cap_shift1")
# Shift 2: 6 AM–noon
model.addConstr(processed[1] <= 60 * (w1 + w2), name="cap_shift2")
# Shift 3: noon–6 PM
model.addConstr(processed[2] <= 60 * (w2 + w3), name="cap_shift3")
# Shift 4: 6 PM–midnight
model.addConstr(processed[3] <= 60 * w3, name="cap_shift4")

# Processed orders + penalty = orders received
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    model.addConstr(processed[i-1] + penalty[i-1] == ord_i, name=f"balance_shift{i}")

# Objective: minimize labor cost ($12 per hour, 12 hours per worker) + penalties
labor_cost = 144 * (w1 + w2 + w3)  # 12 workers * 12 hours * $12
penalty_cost = gp.quicksum(penalty)
model.setObjective(labor_cost + penalty_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if found
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create model with the provided environment
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Orders received in each shift
orders = [150, 250, 400, 300]

# Decision variables: number of workers scheduled for each pair of consecutive shifts
w1 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w1")  # midnight–6 AM & 6 AM–noon
w2 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w2")  # 6 AM–noon & noon–6 PM
w3 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w3")  # noon–6 PM & 6 PM–midnight

# Decision variables: orders processed and penalties for each shift
processed = []
penalty   = []
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    p = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"processed_{i}")
    pr = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"penalty_{i}")
    processed.append(p)
    penalty.append(pr)

# Capacity constraints for each shift
# Shift 1: midnight–6 AM
model.addConstr(processed[0] <= 60 * w1, name="cap_shift1")
# Shift 2: 6 AM–noon
model.addConstr(processed[1] <= 60 * (w1 + w2), name="cap_shift2")
# Shift 3: noon–6 PM
model.addConstr(processed[2] <= 60 * (w2 + w3), name="cap_shift3")
# Shift 4: 6 PM–midnight
model.addConstr(processed[3] <= 60 * w3, name="cap_shift4")

# Processed orders + penalty = orders received
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    model.addConstr(processed[i-1] + penalty[i-1] == ord_i, name=f"balance_shift{i}")

# Objective: minimize labor cost ($12 per hour, 12 hours per worker) + penalties
labor_cost = 144 * (w1 + w2 + w3)  # 12 workers * 12 hours * $12
penalty_cost = gp.quicksum(penalty)
model.setObjective(labor_cost + penalty_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if found
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create model with the provided environment
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Orders received in each shift
orders = [150, 250, 400, 300]

# Decision variables: number of workers scheduled for each pair of consecutive shifts
w1 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w1")  # midnight–6 AM & 6 AM–noon
w2 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w2")  # 6 AM–noon & noon–6 PM
w3 = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="w3")  # noon–6 PM & 6 PM–midnight

# Decision variables: orders processed and penalties for each shift
processed = []
penalty   = []
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    p = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"processed_{i}")
    pr = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=ord_i, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"penalty_{i}")
    processed.append(p)
    penalty.append(pr)

# Capacity constraints for each shift
# Shift 1: midnight–6 AM
model.addConstr(processed[0] <= 60 * w1, name="cap_shift1")
# Shift 2: 6 AM–noon
model.addConstr(processed[1] <= 60 * (w1 + w2), name="cap_shift2")
# Shift 3: noon–6 PM
model.addConstr(processed[2] <= 60 * (w2 + w3), name="cap_shift3")
# Shift 4: 6 PM–midnight
model.addConstr(processed[3] <= 60 * w3, name="cap_shift4")

# Processed orders + penalty = orders received
for i, ord_i in enumerate(orders, start=1):
    model.addConstr(processed[i-1] + penalty[i-1] == ord_i, name=f"balance_shift{i}")

# Objective: minimize labor cost ($12 per hour, 12 hours per worker) + penalties
labor_cost = 144 * (w1 + w2 + w3)  # 12 workers * 12 hours * $12
penalty_cost = gp.quicksum(penalty)
model.setObjective(labor_cost + penalty_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output the optimal objective value if found
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

y_s = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=1000, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="y_s")
x_st = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=1000, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="x_st")
y_st = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=1000, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="y_st")

# Fixed coordinates for Packaging (0,0) and Loading Dock (800,600)
coords = {
    0: (0, 0),          # Packaging
    1: (800, 600),      # Loading Dock
    2: (x_s, y_s),      # Sorting Facility
    3: (x_st, y_st)     # Storage Facility
}

# Trip matrix (directed trips per day)
t = {
    (0, 1): 20, (0, 2): 15, (0, 3): 10,
    (1, 0): 20, (1, 2): 25, (1, 3): 30,
    (2, 0): 15, (2, 1): 25, (2, 3): 40,
    (3, 0): 10, (3, 1): 30, (3, 2): 40
}

# Absolute difference variables for each unordered pair (i<j)
dx = {}
dy = {}
for i in range(4):
    for j in range(i+1, 4):
        dx[(i, j)] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"dx_{i}_{j}")
        dy[(i, j)] = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"dy_{i}_{j}")

# Constraints to enforce absolute differences
for i in range(4):
    for j in range(i+1, 4):
        xi, yi = coords[i]
        xj, yj = coords[j]
        # |xi - xj| constraints
        model.addConstr(dx[(i, j)] >= xi - xj, name=f"dx_ge_{i}_{j}_1")
        model.addConstr(dx[(i, j)] >= xj - xi, name=f"dx_ge_{i}_{j}_2")
        # |yi - yj| constraints
        model.addConstr(dy[(i, j)] >= yi - yj, name=f"dy_ge_{i}_{j}_1")
        model.addConstr(dy[(i, j)] >= yj - yi, name=f"dy_ge_{i}_{j}_2")
        # Minimum distance of 100 units (Manhattan)
        model.addConstr(dx[(i, j)] + dy[(i, j)] >= 100, name=f"min_dist_{i}_{j}")

# Objective: minimize daily transportation cost
cost_expr = 0
for (i, j), trips in t.items():
    # Determine the unordered pair key
    key = (i, j) if i < j else (j, i)
    cost_expr += 0.5 * trips * (dx[key] + dy[key])

model.setObjective(cost_expr, GRB.MINIMIZE)

model.optimize()

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Define sets
tasks = range(1, 11)          # Tasks 1..10
workstations = range(1, 11)   # Workstations 1..10

# Parameters
durations = {
    1: 36,
    2: 36,
    3: 30,
    4: 30,
    5: 24,
    6: 30,
    7: 24,
    8: 12,
    9: 54,
    10: 12
}
cycle_time = 66

# Precedence relations (i precedes j)
precedence = [
    (1, 2),
    (3, 4),
    (1, 5),
    (4, 5),
    (5, 6),
    (2, 7),
    (6, 8),
    (7, 8),
    (8, 9),
    (9, 10)
]

# Create model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(tasks, workstations, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
y = model.addVars(workstations, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="y")

# Each task assigned to exactly one workstation
for i in tasks:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, w] for w in workstations) == 1,
                    name=f"assign_{i}")

# Workstation capacity constraints
for w in workstations:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(durations[i] * x[i, w] for i in tasks) <= cycle_time * y[w],
                    name=f"cap_{w}")

# Precedence constraints
for (i, j) in precedence:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(w * x[i, w] for w in workstations) <=
                    gp.quicksum(w * x[j, w] for w in workstations),
                    name=f"prec_{i}_{j}")

# Linking y with x: a workstation is used if any task is assigned to it
for w in workstations:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, w] for i in tasks) <= len(tasks) * y[w],
                    name=f"link_{w}")

# Objective: minimize number of workstations used
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(y[w] for w in workstations), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Define sets
tasks = range(1, 11)          # Tasks 1..10
workstations = range(1, 11)   # Workstations 1..10

# Parameters
durations = {
    1: 36,
    2: 36,
    3: 30,
    4: 30,
    5: 24,
    6: 30,
    7: 24,
    8: 12,
    9: 54,
    10: 12
}
cycle_time = 66

# Precedence relations (i precedes j)
precedence = [
    (1, 2),
    (3, 4),
    (1, 5),
    (4, 5),
    (5, 6),
    (2, 7),
    (6, 8),
    (7, 8),
    (8, 9),
    (9, 10)
]

# Create model
model = gp.Model(env=env)

# Decision variables
x = model.addVars(tasks, workstations, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
y = model.addVars(workstations, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="y")

# Each task assigned to exactly one workstation
for i in tasks:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, w] for w in workstations) == 1,
                    name=f"assign_{i}")

# Workstation capacity constraints
for w in workstations:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(durations[i] * x[i, w] for i in tasks) <= cycle_time * y[w],
                    name=f"cap_{w}")

# Precedence constraints
for (i, j) in precedence:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(w * x[i, w] for w in workstations) <=
                    gp.quicksum(w * x[j, w] for w in workstations),
                    name=f"prec_{i}_{j}")

# Linking y with x: a workstation is used if any task is assigned to it
for w in workstations:
    model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, w] for i in tasks) <= len(tasks) * y[w],
                    name=f"link_{w}")

# Objective: minimize number of workstations used
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(y[w] for w in workstations), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
model.optimize()

# Output
if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj = gp.quicksum(distances[w][c] * x[w][c] for w in range(3) for c in range(5))

y = [model.addVar(lb=ri, ub=width - ri, name=f"y{i}") for i, ri in enumerate(radii)]

FEW-SHOT DEMONSTRATIONS

EXAMPLE 1
=========

Input
-----
A marketing company allocates nonnegative integer resource units to projects X
and Y. The total allocation cannot exceed 1,000 units. Project X must receive
at least 200 units more than project Y. Project X costs $50 per unit and is
limited to 700 units; project Y costs $30 per unit and is limited to 500 units.
What is the minimum total allocation cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model(env=env)
x = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=700, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")
y = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=500, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="y")
model.addConstr(x + y <= 1000, name="total_allocation")
model.addConstr(x - y >= 200, name="required_excess")
model.setObjective(50 * x + 30 * y, GRB.MINIMIZE)
model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

EXAMPLE 2
=========

Input
-----
An energy company chooses nonnegative integer numbers of solar and wind
projects. A solar project costs 7 units and a wind project costs 5 units. The
portfolio must satisfy 2 solar + 3 wind >= 10, while grid capacity requires
4 solar + wind <= 15. What is the minimum total investment cost?

Expected response
-----------------
```python
import gurobipy as gp

solar = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="solar")
wind = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="wind")
model.addConstr(2 * solar + 3 * wind >= 10, name="minimum_output")
model.addConstr(4 * solar + wind <= 15, name="grid_capacity")

model.optimize()

if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"FINAL_OBJECTIVE={model.ObjVal:.17g}")
```

edges = [
    (0, 1, 12),
    (0, 2, 8),
    (1, 2, 5),
    (1, 3, 9),

    (3, 4, 6),
    (3, 5, 11),
    (4, 6, 10),
    (5, 6, 4),
    (5, 7, 8),
    (6, 8, 7),
    (7, 8, 6),
]
